summary: Backend-only testing of new VitaGuide-Scores engine endpoints under /api/wearable/*: baselines, scores, timeseries. Created /app/backend/tests/test_wearable_scoring.py with 13 pytest cases across 4 classes (TestBaselines, TestScores, TestTimeseries, TestEstimateMetadata). All 13 tests passed (100%). Verified: 28-day rolling median baselines with correct per-metric fields (median, days_used, sufficient, latest_value, delta_pct); sufficient=false when <7 days (seeded 3 days) and sufficient=true when >=7 days (seeded 8 days); learning-phase gating on /scores with null values + German lernt-note when days_of_data<7; valid 0-100 recovery/sleep/activity/readiness numbers when >=7 days; beta=true on every score bucket; 400 on invalid date and invalid range; /timeseries?range=week returns granularity='daily' with points+stats{avg,min,max,days}; /timeseries?range=day returns granularity='raw' with individual samples; /scores.baselines equals /baselines output; scoring is deterministic across repeat calls; blood_glucose_estimated + blood_pressure_systolic get metadata.estimate=true and metadata.disclaimer auto-injected on POST /measurements/batch even when client omits metadata, while heart_rate does NOT.
critical_code_review_comments: wearable_scoring.compute_user_baselines uses ISO string comparison (measured_at >= since) — measurements written with mixed timezones or naive strings can be silently included/excluded. Normalise measured_at to UTC on ingest.

compute_scores_for_date recomputes baselines and re-scans distinct measured_at on every call; for /timeseries+/scores on the dashboard this can be O(N) repeated. Consider caching baselines per (user_id, date) or precomputing nightly.

delta_pct in baselines is computed on latest_day median vs 28-day median — when days_used == 1 the latest equals the median so delta_pct == 0.0, which reads as 'no change' rather than 'insufficient'. Consider returning delta_pct=null until sufficient=true.

_readiness_score gates on 'recovery is None or sleep is None' but recovery requires HRV/RHR baselines. If a user provides only sleep+activity, readiness stays null even though partial-readiness could be surfaced. Consider soft-fallback.

scoring_config.json readiness weights sum to 0.45+0.30-0.10+0.25+0.10 = 1.00 only if activity_yesterday_load subtracts; but the code computes w['activity_yesterday_load'] * _clamp(load,0,1) (a subtraction because the weight itself is negative). This double-negation is subtle — worth documenting or renaming key to 'activity_load_penalty'.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral users 'e2e-scoring-<8hex>': one with 3 days (insufficient) of measurements + one with 8 days of measurements & sleep sessions + one empty user + one for estimate-metadata check. All devices purged with purge_data=true in teardown fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New scoring layer (baselines/scores/timeseries) is green. If UI onboarding surfaces the learning-phase note or renders /timeseries charts, next iteration should add Playwright coverage for those views. Estimate-disclaimer enforcement is already covered here (previously flagged as untested in it_91).
